questions.q: What does Fabric's Git integration actually sync to a repository?
options: Each item's definition — a notebook's cells, a pipeline's activity graph, a model's relationships — as real, diffable files
The actual raw data sitting in OneLake
Only Warehouse tables, never Lakehouse tables
Nothing; Git integration only tracks workspace permissions
questions.explain: Item definitions get committed as real files; the underlying data never does.

questions.q: Why does Git integration never track the actual trip data sitting in a lakehouse?
options: Version control here means tracking how a pipeline or model is built, not backing up the underlying data itself
Git integration is technically incapable of tracking any file larger than 1MB
Lakehouse data is automatically excluded by a hardcoded Fabric limitation with no design reasoning
OneLake data is never actually stored in files at all
questions.explain: This mirrors the same distinction Databricks & Delta Lake's Chapter 2 drew between a table's schema/logic and its actual Parquet files.

questions.q: What does a Fabric deployment pipeline do?
options: Promotes a workspace's items through real dev, test, and production stages, each its own workspace
Deletes items from a workspace after a set retention period
Only applies to semantic models, never notebooks or pipelines
Replaces the need for Git integration entirely
questions.explain: This is the same environment-separation instinct as Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 47's catalog-per-environment practice.

questions.q: How does Fabric's Git integration compare in scope to what Databricks & Delta Lake covered?
options: It's a workspace-wide sync covering every item type at once, genuinely broader than that course's notebook-focused Lakeflow material
It's narrower, only covering notebooks and nothing else
The two are functionally identical in every respect
Databricks & Delta Lake never mentioned version control at all
questions.explain: This is described as a genuine gap/expansion, worth noting directly rather than assuming exact parity.

questions.q: Where does this course return to the Git/CI-CD idea with fuller production-practice treatment?
options: Lesson 45, much later in the course
Never — this lesson is the only coverage of the topic
Lesson 2, immediately after this one
Only in the separate Data Factory course, not this one
questions.explain: This lesson previews the concept; the later production chapter dedicates a full lesson to CI/CD specifically.
